statement.p: If z = xe^{y},\qquad x = u^{2}-v^{2},\qquad y = u^{2}+v^{2}, find \partial z/\partial u and \partial z/\partial v. The variables are restricted to domains on which the functions are defined.

static.solution: z is a function of two variables x and y which are functions of two variables the two chain rule identities which apply are: \frac{\partial z}{\partial u} = \frac{\partial z}{\partial x}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}+ \frac{\partial z}{\partial y}\frac{\partial y}{\partial u} = (e^{y}) \left(2u\right) + (xe^{y})\cdot\left(2u\right) = e^{u^{2}+v^{2}}\cdot 2u+\left(u^{2}-v^{2}\right)e^{u^{2}+v^{2}}\cdot 2u. and \frac{\partial z}{\partial v} = \frac{\partial z}{\partial x}\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}+ \frac{\partial z}{\partial y}\frac{\partial y}{\partial v} = (e^{y})\left(-\left(2v\right)\right) + (xe^{y})\cdot \left(2v\right) = \left(u^{2}-v^{2}\right)e^{u^{2}+v^{2}}\cdot 2v-e^{u^{2}+v^{2}}\cdot 2v.
